user.title: Vimar Intercom
user.description:
On the indoor unit, open Settings → Network and devices → Mobile device pairing, and pick a free slot: the unit pairs up to ten devices and shows the QR code for the slot you pick. Take a photo or a screenshot of the QR code and upload it here. If you have the QR code as text instead, paste it.

Give Home Assistant a slot of its own, not the one your phone uses: each slot has its own SIP identity, and sharing one with a phone or another system can knock both offline.

Home Assistant reads and decrypts the QR code locally, deletes the image straight away, and keeps only the credentials in this config entry.

data.qr_payload: Or paste the QR code text

confirm.title: Confirm the panel

reconfigure.title: Update the QR code
reconfigure.description: On the indoor unit, open Settings → Network and devices → Mobile device pairing and pick the slot Home Assistant uses; the unit shows that slot's QR code. Upload a photo or a screenshot of it, or paste its text. The existing device identity is kept so the Vimar cloud still recognises this installation.

data.qr_payload: Or paste the QR code text

error.invalid_qr: That QR code is not a Vimar one, or it is incomplete. Use the QR code the indoor unit shows under Settings → Network and devices → Mobile device pairing; if you pasted text, copy the whole string, including any trailing '=' characters.
error.no_qr_input: Upload an image of the QR code, or paste its text.
error.qr_not_found: No QR code was found in that image. Use a sharp, straight-on photo or a screenshot with the whole QR code in view, or paste the text instead.
error.multiple_qr: That image contains more than one QR code. Crop it to the one from the indoor unit and upload it again.
error.image_unreadable: That image could not be read. Upload it again as a PNG or JPEG, or paste the text instead.
error.image_heic: That is a HEIC photo, which Home Assistant cannot open. Take a screenshot of the QR code, or export the photo as JPEG, and upload that instead.
error.image_too_large: That image is too large. Upload a screenshot or a smaller photo of the QR code.
error.qr_reader_unavailable: This Home Assistant installation cannot read QR images: the zbar library is missing. Paste the QR code text instead.

abort.already_configured: This intercom is already set up.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one Vimar intercom can be set up.
abort.wrong_panel: That QR code belongs to a different panel. Remove the existing entry first.

init.title: Vimar Intercom options
init.description: Entrance panels, door locks and the other actuators are discovered automatically from the phonebook the indoor unit publishes, with the names set on it; nothing here needs changing then. The panel list and the door command below are used only when the phonebook cannot be downloaded (some plant types, or the Vimar cloud unreachable at first setup). Panel addresses are the SIP extensions of your entrance panels, comma separated. Add ':Name' to label one, for example '55001:Street Gate, 55002:Building Door'. The door command also picks which phonebook door keeps the original door lock's entity.

data.prefer_local: Prefer the panel on the local network

error.invalid_panels: Panel addresses must be numeric SIP extensions, comma separated.
error.invalid_door_command: The door open command must be letters, digits and underscores only, for example OPEN_2F. It is sent to the panel exactly as written.

registration_down.title: Vimar Intercom is not registered
registration_down.description: The intercom has not been registered with the Vimar cloud for more than five minutes, so the doorbell will not ring in Home Assistant. Home Assistant keeps retrying. Check that the panel is online and that this host can reach {proxy_host} on port {proxy_port}.

migration_required.title: Vimar Intercom must be set up again
migration_required.description: This Home Assistant was using Vimar Intercom 1.x, and version 2 cannot reuse its configuration: the credentials used to be edited into the integration's source and now come from a QR code the indoor unit generates, which Home Assistant cannot fetch for you. The intercom will not work until you do this: go to Settings > Devices & services, delete the Vimar Intercom entry, then add the integration again and upload the QR code generated on the indoor unit (Settings > Network and devices > Mobile device pairing). Most entity IDs change; see the integration's README before rewriting your automations.
